_meta.description: DHM Nepal hydrological stations on the Bhote Koshi-Trishuli-Narayani corridor, with official warning/danger thresholds and their state during the 26 August 2026 event.
_meta._verification_note: Rebuilt 1 Sept from the DHM river-watch ten-minute series. Two corrections followed. The corridor has two Bhote Koshi stations, one at Rasuwagadhi and one at Syabrubesi, and this package previously carried a single record fusing them: the Rasuwagadhi station's stage and thresholds under the Syabrubesi name, with the Syabrubesi station's cessation time. A fifth silent station, Phalakhu Khola at Betrawati, was not in the report's list of four. Front arrival times are now read from the series rather than from the report's prose.
_meta._source: Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, Flood Forecasting Division (बाढी पूर्वानुमान महाशाखा), Babarmahal, Kathmandu. Technical situation report on the 2083 Bhote Koshi-Trishuli-Narayani flood, 2083 Bhadra 10 (26 August 2026), 9 pp.
_meta._secondary_source: https://www.dhm.gov.np/hydrology/hms-Single/{station_id} and its getRiverWatchBySeriesId_Single endpoint, retrieved by analysis/fetch_dhm_series.py into data/gauge_timeseries.json
_meta._grade: A1 for the instrument series, A2 for the situation report
_meta._station_index_confirmed: The department's own correspondence of 3 September 2026 refers to station 449.91 as Trishuli at Kali Khola and station 450 as Narayani at Devghat, and states that Galchi has no station number. Those are the station_index values recorded here, and Galchhi's is empty, so the identification this package rebuilt from the river-watch service agrees with the department's own numbering.
_meta._silence_note: still_silent_as_of stays at 2 September 2026, the last date the service's retention window reached when that check was made. A re-query on 9 September found the four stations still returning nothing, but retention had rolled forward past the dates needed to extend the observation, so the earlier date is the last one the record supports.

stations.note: Gauges absolute water level rather than stage above a local datum, so its 367 m threshold and 369.45 m peak are elevations. Rose 8.8 m above its pre-wave level and crossed its threshold at 10:40. This station supplies the measured arrival that replaces the forecast time carried earlier.

stations.name: Trishuli at Phurke Khola (Malekhu)
stations.coord_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (settlement centroid, not surveyed station position)
stations.note: Only in-path station that crossed its thresholds before being destroyed. Station and the adjacent bridge were swept away immediately after 11:43.
stations._chronology_contradiction: The 11:40 live-station reading of 10.48 m is already 2.48 m above the 8.0 m danger threshold, yet the sitrep logs the danger crossing at 11:43, three minutes later. The two come from different sources (live station JSON, grade B1; sitrep, grade A2) and cannot both be right. Most likely the 11:43 entry marks the destruction of the station and bridge rather than the threshold crossing. The manuscript therefore does not describe the second detachment as following the danger crossing by two minutes.
stations._front_arrival_note: Front arrival at this node is taken as the 11:26 warning crossing, not the 11:50 'flood reaches Malekhu bazaar' entry. The gauge is co-located with the settlement, so 11:50 is a later confirmation and using it understates celerity on the Betrawati-Malekhu reach and produces a spurious non-monotonic profile.
stations._source: DHM technical situation report. The river-watch service exposes no series for this station, so it is the one corridor gauge still taken from the report.

resolved_to_instruments.Rasuwa Syabrubesi: Bhote Koshi at Shyaprubesi, station 191, silent after 08:50

stations_destroyed._fifth_station: Phalakhu Khola at Betrawati, station 4658, went silent after 09:20 in the same ten-minute window as the Trishuli station beside it and has not reported since. It is not in the report's list of four. It gauges a tributary, so it is excluded from the flow-path analysis and counted only as a telemetry signal.
stations_destroyed._count_definition: Stations on or adjacent to the corridor that stopped reporting on 26 August and had not resumed by 2 September. Four are named by DHM; the fifth is visible only in the feed. Phurke is reported washed away but exposes no series, so its silence cannot be confirmed the same way.

_threshold_summary._source: Computed from the station records in this file
_threshold_summary._gradient: Along the main stem the fraction rises downstream, 0.27 at Rasuwagadhi, 0.69 at Syabrubesi and 0.87 at Betrawati. Every one of the four was destroyed below its own warning stage, so a threshold-triggered system would have produced no alert from any of them.
_threshold_summary._supersedes: This package previously recorded three destroyed stations with published thresholds and two below their warning stage, because two instruments were held as one record and the Rasuwagadhi station was thought to have no published threshold. It has one: 6.0 m warning, 7.0 m danger.

telemetry_loss_as_a_signal._source: Cessation times from the DHM river-watch series; the operational objection from an external practitioner review of the preprint, 30 August 2026.
telemetry_loss_as_a_signal._grade: A1 for the timings, expert opinion for the objection
telemetry_loss_as_a_signal._finding: The two uppermost stations fall silent ten minutes apart, not thirty. A rule acting on one missing report could have fired at 08:50, ten minutes before the Division was notified and twenty-six before the public alert. A rule requiring two stations on the same stem could have fired at 09:00, at the same moment the human relay reached the Division and sixteen minutes before the alert. Coincidence detection therefore costs ten minutes against single-station triggering on this event, rather than being unavailable.
telemetry_loss_as_a_signal._supersedes: The earlier record put the two documented losses thirty minutes apart with the second falling after the public alert, and concluded that a coincidence rule could not have fired in time. That rested on the fused station record, which hid the 08:40 loss at Rasuwagadhi. With both Bhote Koshi stations separated the coincidence was available, and the question this package previously recorded as undeterminable is answered.
telemetry_loss_as_a_signal._independence_caveat: The false-alarm advantage of coincidence detection assumes station failures are independent. Stations sharing power or transmission backhaul are not, and monsoon conditions that produce the hazard also stress the communications, so failures may be positively correlated with the event the detector is meant to catch. The Phalakhu and Trishuli stations at Betrawati going silent in the same ten-minute window is consistent either with one flood destroying both or with a shared backhaul failing once. No topology or outage history for the DHM network is public, so the assumption still cannot be tested.
telemetry_loss_as_a_signal._consequence: The manuscript's telemetry passage is rewritten again: the coincidence rule is now shown to have been available, with its cost stated in minutes.
